findings.title: Reject concatenated signatures with an unexpected length
findings.body: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies only the first signLength bytes without checking signature.length. An otherwise valid JOSE ECDSA signature with arbitrary bytes appended therefore produces exactly the same DER signature and can still verify successfully. JOSE requires the exact fixed signature length; accepting these inputs permits token/signature malleability. Check the input length and throw IOException before copying (also avoiding unchecked array-copy exceptions for short inputs).

findings.title: Exercise the actual ES384 and ES512 curves and verify the reconstructed signature
findings.body: All three tests generate an EC key using the provider's default curve (normally P-256), including testES384 and testES512. Changing the hash algorithm does not change the curve, so these tests only pad P-256 integers to larger lengths and never exercise real P-384 or P-521 signatures, including the long-form DER sequence length needed for P-521. Moreover, comparing two concatenated conversions can pass when the first conversion loses data. Generate the appropriate curve for each algorithm and verify the reconstructed DER signature against the original data and public key.
